_note: Sound design under the voice, in three independent layers with one field each. PLACE -> `rules`: the script's per-segment `scene` label picks a rule (first match wins, ordered specific -> general) and the rule names effect TAGS, matched against assets/effect-pool.json. MOOD -> `music_palette`: the script's per-segment `music` value is a key of the palette, and the palette names the tags for assets/music-pool.json. The two are deliberately separate fields: a place is where we are, a mood is what it feels like, and one string doing both is how a shop at dawn came out with a hearth under it. A rule names tags, never files, so adding a clip to a pool is how the mix gains a new sound. `level` is a linear gain over a clip normalized to -26 LUFS, so it means the same thing for every clip. `pause_before_s` is a beat held before this scene's first line, in delivered seconds — see the `pause` block. Every knob these layers read lives here and nowhere else.

music_palette._note: The closed vocabulary the digest may emit as a segment's `music`. Closed on purpose: a free-text mood label matched by keyword is how 345 scene labels ended up fighting 14 rules. Every value but `none` must be answerable by a clip in assets/music-pool.json, so 'this mood has no track' cannot happen — and if a pool loses its last clip for a mood, that stretch is simply silent rather than filled with something wrong. This block is what build_prompt injects into prompts/analyze.txt, so the prompt and the pool cannot drift apart.

quiet.note: low and unobtrusive — the default under narration, reflection, ordinary talk

warm.note: hearth, home, tavern, friendly company, a meal

grand.note: triumph, revelation, awe, a turning point

playful.note: humor, games, light mischief, warm comedy

none.note: silence — a death, a shock, a line that must land dry

legacy_scene_music._note: Migration shim, not the design. Scripts digested before segments carried `music` are scored by the old keyword rules over their `scene` label; this is that mapping, in the old rule order, each old music-tag set reduced to the nearest palette value. Where the old tags answered no clip at all — `tense` for storms, `dark` for caves, which is why those scenes were silent before — it maps to `none`, so a re-merge reproduces the old intent rather than inventing music the chapter never had. It exists so the ~200 chapters already on disk keep merging; a freshly digested script declares `music` per segment and never reads this. Delete the block once every script on disk carries the field.

layers._note: effect: the layer that must stay sparse. A window opens on a scene that names effect tags and lasts at least min_span_s, is clipped to max_window_s, waits cooldown_s of silence after the previous window closed, and the chapter may not spend more than max_coverage of its runtime on the layer. `trim` is the layer's one master gain, multiplied into each rule's own `level`: a rule's `level` says how a storm balances against a hearth, `trim` says the whole layer is too hot, and keeping those separate is what makes retuning it one edit instead of thirteen. music: continuous, deliberately below the effect layer's loud scenes, lifted to pause_level inside a planned pause. ramp_s is how long that lift takes and must stay well under the shortest pause, or the lift never arrives. xfade_s is the crossfade where the track changes — and a track changes exactly where the script changes its `music` value, so that knob is what makes an in-chapter change audible as a change rather than a cut. inject: spot effects the script places itself — a hit holds its whole clip as silence, an overlap costs no time and runs under the following speech, a trail holds `default_hold_s` solo and tails under it; a stop fades a running tail over `stop_fade_s` (3 s — a shorter fade reads as a cut), a retrigger over `fade_s`, a natural tail-end over `tail_fade_s` (1 s, clamped to half the clip — a tail, not a third of the sound); a `looped` bed is filled by repeating the clip with a `loop_xfade_s` crossfade at each seam. NOTE ON `speed`: the merge tempoes the SPEECH only, then places both layers against the delivered clock, so nothing here is ever heard at atempo.

pause._note: A beat is held before a scene's first line only where a scene change is narrated: the incoming or outgoing turn must be the Narrator, and narration resuming (incoming) beats narration handing off. At most max_per_chapter of them; the longest declared pause_before_s wins, ties go to the earliest. The duration is in DELIVERED seconds — the merge scales it by `speed` before writing it, so a 1.5 s beat is still 1.5 s at atempo 1.25. Keep it comfortably longer than duck.release (400 ms): the music's lift inside the pause IS the sidechain releasing, so a beat shorter than the release never lifts at all.

duck._note: One sidechain compressor, keyed on the voice track, applied to both layers as a single bus — so 'every layer drops whenever anyone speaks' is a property of the signal path rather than a rule each layer has to remember. The key is the whole voice track, which is why the narrator ducks them exactly as a character does.
